gen-gf-unica-one-fs-karma: Commanding, Unica One keeps every stroke uniform, with a very large lowercase eye and daylight inside each curve. Karma moves through a paragraph with a gentle modulation that never snags the eye, trustworthy and classic.
gen-irish-grover-fs-karma: Irish Grover is fun and organic, its sturdy oversized lowercase and softly varied strokes giving words real presence. But Karma's trustworthy steadiness is what holds the pair together, its terminals finishing well away from the stem.
gen-irish-grover-general-sans: Fun and organic, Irish Grover sits between monoline and hairline strokes, with sturdy, generous lowercase. And General Sans does what Irish Grover can't: bend smoothly, like letters shaped from a single wire.
gen-mystery-quest-satoshi: Nostalgic and bookish, Mystery Quest keeps open jaws on its curves and compact ascenders over its lowercase. But Satoshi does the approachable work, with a lofty x-height and uniform strokes like a technical pen.
gen-audiowide-gf-cascadia-code: Futuristic tiles with wide grout lines: Audiowide has no thick-thin shift and a lowercase that towers over its capitals. Cascadia Code keeps a wire-like monoline skeleton, with neighbors spaced far enough apart to notice.
gen-audiowide-gf-cascadia-mono: Futuristic and tech-minded, Audiowide lays glyphs out like tiles. Cascadia Mono stands letters like pins in a wide board, and its curves match its stems in weight, just as Audiowide's do.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-asap: Commanding and playful, Early GameBoy stretches its tracking wide and lifts its lowercase skyward, with only a modest thick-thin difference. Asap steadies the page beneath it with open, readable arcs.
gen-tourney-fs-supreme: Athletic and bold, Tourney builds every stroke uniform, stretches words with wide tracking, and bulks up its small letters. Give Supreme a modest size and its crisp, open letters hold up.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-fs-asap: Adventure in wide strides: Eight Bit Dragon spaces its letters generously, with towering lowercase and a small, steady shift in stroke thickness. Asap handles readability, with open arcs and near-capital height.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans brings big, sturdy lowercase and an e whose eye opens clearly to the right. Merriweather Sans backs up Edo SZ, whose cast-iron lowercase holds one constant stroke width.
